name: import-chrome-from-the-pane
description: The import pane previews the staged Chrome fixture and imports it. With Settings still open, the Engines pane already lists the imported engines, so a later edit there cannot save the old list. Settings then closes, the sidebar gains the Personal space, and a reopened Settings still counts the same Chrome files and still lists the engines from disk. The Chrome folder is the hand-built fixture in fixtures/import/chrome/basic.

actions.note: Atrium frontmost, or cmd+comma opens Finder Settings

actions.expression: (() => { const item = document.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="import"]'); if (!item) { return 'no import rail item'; } item.click(); return 'clicked'; })()

actions.note: evidence: the Chrome card with its counts, light mode

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.import-card[data-source="chrome"] .import-run'); if (!b) { return 'no button'; } b.click(); return 'clicked'; })()

actions.note: the run answered while Settings is open

actions.expression: (() => { const item = document.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="engines"]'); if (!item) { return 'no rail'; } item.click(); return [...document.querySelectorAll('.engine-row .engine-keyword')].some((k) => k.textContent === 'wiki') ? 'wiki' : 'missing'; })()
actions.note: the open page took the saved settings, so its next save keeps the imported engines
evidence: the imported engines in the live Engines pane
the Default profile's Chrome space reaches the sidebar; hint-triggers.js parks a dot's native title into aria-label, so title itself is always empty

actions.expression: (() => { const item = document.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="import"]'); if (!item) { return 'no rail'; } item.click(); return document.querySelector('.import-card[data-source="chrome"] .import-counts') ? 'card' : 'waiting'; })()
actions.note: a wait_vlog would match the first window's lines, so this polls the reopened page

actions.expression: (() => { const item = document.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="engines"]'); if (!item) { return 'no rail'; } item.click(); return [...document.querySelectorAll('.engine-row .engine-keyword')].some((k) => k.textContent === 'wiki') ? 'wiki' : 'missing'; })()
actions.note: the reopened window read settings.json from disk

"2 spaces, 8 tabs, 3 search engines and 2 profiles"
